children: dropped more than 20% in the premarket on Wednesday as investors reacted to initial results from a Phase 2 trial for its lead candidate, dabogratinib, in patients with a type of bladder cancer.

The SURF302 trial was designed to evaluate dabogratinib in FGFR3-altered low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, a tumor characterized by frequent recurrence and for which current treatment options include intravesical chemotherapy after tumor resection.
Citing an August 31 data cut, Tyra
said the once-daily oral therapy indicated a favorable safety profile.

However, 14% and 9% of those in the 60 mg QD and 50 mg QD dose cohorts experienced Grade 3 treatment-emergent adverse events. While no Grade 4 or 5 TEAEs were recorded, nearly 5% of patients across both cohorts reported Grade 3 treatment-related AEs.

Regarding the trial’s main endpoints, the company disclosed a 100% overall response rate and a 75% best overall response CR rate in reaction to 60 mg QD in single-marker lesion patients whose disease most closely resembles the adjuvant setting.

title: Tyra drops after mid-stage trial data for lead asset in bladder cancer
